Header: Fusarium oxysporum f.sp. cubense Kunyala kwa nthochi

Prevention: Use of disease free planting materials from uninfected fields
Use tissue cultured planting materials available from
LUANAR Avoid planting on sites with a previous history of the disease
Restrict movement of suckers from disease bananas in infected areas to clean areas
The disease is soil borne - avoid moving soils from infected areas
Sterilize tools after handling diseased plants
Restrict movement of people into infected fields to avoid moving the contaminated soil and infected plants into disease free areas
Improve drainage - this disease is more severe in poorly drained soils
Monitoring: Monitor plants weekly for disease symptoms
The first symptoms are faint green/pale-yellow streaks at the base of the petioles on the oldest leaves
The oldest leaves turn yellow around the edges then spreading to the whole leaf
The leaves then collapse and hang down against the stem, turn brown and dry.
Only the youngest partially furled leaves remain upright.
Yellowing progresses from oldest to youngest
Observe leaf sheath with longitudinal splits at the base of pseudostem
Cut open and look for discouloured, purple, reddish or blackened vascular bundles in the pseudostem and corm
Take action when the first symptoms are seen
Direct Control: Destroy infected pseudostem, corms and leaves by burying or drying and burning
Restrictions: There are currently no chemical controls recommended for this disease in
